title: Uploading files
description: Send multipart data directly to your conversion server.

sections.title: Upload fields
table: A binary file with a recognizable filename extension.
Target format ID, such as webp.
Optional JSON object with conversion controls.

sections.title: Submit the request
paragraphs: Let curl or FormData set the Content-Type boundary. The total multipart request, including overhead, must fit within 25 MiB. The server accepts four uploads at once.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: The server checks the filename extension, target, installed conversion route, and controls before creating a job. Unsupported routes return 422. Paths and arbitrary codec arguments are rejected.

sections.title: Use a recognizable extension
paragraphs: Input format detection uses the uploaded file’s filename extension. Supply photo.png rather than an extensionless name when constructing a File or multipart upload. A content-type hint is not a substitute for that name.
The server does not expose the original filename in public job responses. It converts from private temporary paths and returns a generic attachment filename for the result.

sections.title: Attach conversion controls
paragraphs: options is a JSON string, not separate multipart fields for each control. Let FormData set the multipart boundary; manually setting Content-Type without a matching boundary prevents the server from parsing the body.
